adjudications.evidence_summary: The implementation removes timezone information from both aware datetimes with replace(tzinfo=None) before comparison. Targeted probes reproduced both failure directions: an already-expired token was reported valid, and a still-valid token was reported expired, while direct aware-datetime comparisons returned the opposite and correct results.
adjudications.scope_assessment: The failure is in the supplied is_token_expired implementation and applies to its supported datetime inputs when callers provide aware values with different UTC offsets; the implementation comment explicitly anticipates values from different zones.
adjudications.materiality_assessment: Incorrect expiration decisions can accept expired credentials or prematurely reject valid credentials, materially affecting security and production correctness.

findings.claim: Token expiration is evaluated using local wall-clock fields instead of absolute instants, so callers using different timezone offsets can accept already-expired tokens or reject still-valid tokens.
evidence: evals/cases/case_10/src/tokens.py removes timezone information from expires_at and now with replace(tzinfo=None), discarding their UTC offsets before comparison.
With expires_at=2026-08-28T13:00:00+02:00 (11:00 UTC) and now=2026-08-28T12:00:00+00:00, is_token_expired returned false even though the aware-datetime comparison now >= expires_at was true.
With expires_at=2026-08-28T12:00:00+00:00 and now=2026-08-28T13:00:00+02:00 (11:00 UTC), is_token_expired returned true even though the aware-datetime comparison now >= expires_at was false.
